title: Zapata Quantum and University of Maryland Launch ForShor.ai Formal Verification Challenge for AI-Assisted Quantum Algorithm Design - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Zapata Quantum and the University of Maryland launched ForShor.ai, an open challenge where humans and AI agents submit recursive arithmetic policies for Shor/Regev factoring subroutines that a Lean 4 harness formally verifies before Qualtran resource estimation. The aim is to make AI-discovered quantum circuit optimizations machine-checked, inspectable and reusable, including in Zapata's Quantum Pilot platform.

insights.claim: Zapata Quantum (OTCQB: ZPTA) and the University of Maryland launched ForShor.ai, an open challenge where human researchers and AI agents submit recursive arithmetic schedules for quantum factoring subroutines to a public leaderboard verified by an automated Lean 4 harness.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Positions Zapata at the intersection of AI agents and fault-tolerant quantum software; small-cap ZPTA news flow.
insights.locator: Zapata Quantum (OTCQB: ZPTA) and the University of Maryland

insights.claim: In ForShor, any submitted policy that passes four kernel-checked conditions automatically inherits machine-checked proofs of Shor order-finding success probability and subcubic gate scaling, so the surrounding modular exponentiation logic need not be re-proved.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A reusable pattern for trusting AI-generated code: constrain the search space so correctness proofs come for free — applicable beyond quantum.
insights.locator: Rather than treating AI-generated quantum circuits as opaque black boxes

insights.claim: Exact exhaustive policy search for 2048-bit factoring at arity k=8 would require at least 7.5×10^3 GiB of memory and about 3.2×10^51 core-hours, which is the stated motivation for AI-guided/agentic search.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Illustrates why AI search is needed for quantum compiler optimization — a niche demand driver for AI-for-science tooling.

insights.claim: ForShor's verified circuits lowered to Qualtran estimate 1.685×10^12 T-gates for n=2048 using varying arity k=(6,5,3), with the approach crossing Gidney–Ekerå discrete-log factoring at about 3.8×10^6 bits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Provides a formally verified data point in the ongoing debate over how many resources breaking RSA-2048 requires — relevant to PQC migration urgency.

insights.claim: The Lean 4 harness comprises about 180 files (~3,500 declarations, Apache 2.0) formalizing recursive Toom–Cook PhaseProduct and Cooley–Tukey QFT, and proves O(n^(2+ε)) elementary gate scaling.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: An open-source formal-methods asset that could become a standard reference for verified quantum arithmetic.

insights.claim: The six-week ForShor challenge, covering PhaseProduct (Shor) and PhaseTripleProduct (Regev), serves as a proving ground for formal verification capabilities in Zapata's Quantum Pilot software platform.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Watch whether formal verification becomes a differentiated, monetizable feature of Quantum Pilot.
